solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foreign noble at a fine high-class French palace

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange or altered, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class, high-class

explanation.surface: An aristocrat from abroad is at a stylish upmarket palace in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' looks like it describes the noble but signals the anagram, giving FONTAINEBLE; U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fontainebleau is a famous royal château south-east of Paris, so it is a palace in France.

clue.text: First pair of thespians engaged in leading role, mainly

indicators.note: something engaged in another is held within it, so the pair sits inside the next word

parts.note: leading means foremost, at the front

indicators.note: the first pair of a word is its opening two letters, here taken from thespians

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: The two top actors have taken the lead role, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' puts the pair inside the word for leading, splitting it after FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for the most part is an idiom meaning largely or in general, the same as mainly.

clue.text: Synthetic polymer unknown in northern half of capital

indicators.note: the unknown letter goes in among the letters that follow, between N and the rest
half of the capital keeps only the first three of its six letters

parts.note: London is the UK capital
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, alongside x and z

explanation.surface: An artificial plastic turns up as an unknown quantity in the north of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' keeps the first half of London; Y, a maths unknown, sits just after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a man-made polyamide, a classic example of a synthetic polymer used in fibres.

clue.text: Tree a woman planted outside new councillor's office

parts.note: the alder is a tree

indicators.note: planted outside says the woman's name is set around the following letter

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A tree that a woman planted beyond new council offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted outside' makes MANRY; an aldermanry was also a ward of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldermanry is the rank or post of an alderman, a senior councillor, so it is that councillor's office.

clue.text: Teachers meeting with old actor: that bears fruit

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Teachers meet a veteran actor, which proves fruitful.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT is a former British teachers' union; Tree is the actor Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut tree, such as a hazel or walnut, is a plant that produces nuts, its fruit.

clue.text: A snag over admitting curtailment of party spirit

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the shortened party goes inside the reversed letters
in a down clue over means turned upward, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a snag or obstacle, as in there's the rub

indicators.note: curtailing something cuts off its tail, so the party loses its final letter

parts.note: a rave is a lively party

explanation.surface: There is a snag in letting in a cut-short party spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns the snag letters round to BURA; 'curtailment of' docks the party to RAV, which 'admitting' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravura means great daring or brilliance of style, so it is a kind of spirit or dash.

clue.text: Mutton graduate gives girl

parts.note: printers called the em quad a mutton to tell it apart from the en, or nut
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate's mutton dish is given to a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Mutton is old printers' slang for an em, a unit of type width.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a female first name, so it is a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Rash old city teacher primarily in charge of some music?

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of teacher is used

parts.note: an aria is a piece of music, a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A reckless ancient city teacher is chiefly in charge of the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective meaning hasty but is the noun, a skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is hives, an itchy raised skin eruption, so it is a medical name for a rash.

clue.text: Teacher takes train, overcoming motorway tension

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another comes before it, so the train sits above the rest

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written here as MI
stress is tension

explanation.surface: A teacher catches a train, beating the stress of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, London to Leeds, is the classic crossword motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a female teacher in a school, a dated but standard term.

clue.text: Governed as certain lines may be

explanation.surface: Governed, as some lines of authority are.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled is both past tense of rule, to govern, and an adjective for paper marked with straight lines.

clue.text: Shocking weapon to put out by extremities of tower

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces are set side by side
the extremities of a word are its first and last letters, taken from tower
put out means ejected, so the word to is removed from the weapon

parts.note: an automatic is a self-loading gun

explanation.surface: A shocking gun is set aside beside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' leaves AUMATIC, and 'by' sets the tower's outer letters beside it; 'Shocking' is the definition, not a description of the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traumatic causes deep distress, so it is shocking in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Payment hard old woman initially invested in drink

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
Nora is a woman's name

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the drink

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of invested is used

explanation.surface: A tough old woman put her first payment into drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' supplies its own first letter, and 'in' is the containment signal, giving RIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorarium is a fee given for professional services nominally free, so it is a payment.

clue.text: Repeat part of speech occasionally

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Repeat a fragment of something said now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo something is to say it again or reproduce it, so it means repeat.

clue.text: Flaw in flyers plugging this writer's point

parts.note: this writer's means I am, shortened to I'M

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so the flyers fill the space inside the other letters

parts.note: airmen are flyers

explanation.surface: There's a flaw in the pilots filling this writer's point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugging' sets the flyers between IMP and T; 'this writer' is the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: An impairment is a weakness or defect, so it is a flaw.

clue.text: Humdrum character given note by European national

parts.note: mu is a letter, a character, of the Greek alphabet
a Dane is a citizen of Denmark

explanation.surface: A dull person is handed a note by someone from Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humdrum character' reads as a dull person, but 'character' is the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means ordinary and uninteresting, a close synonym of humdrum.

clue.text: Negative thinkers sit in his complex outside Lima

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters go around the letter that follows
complex means intricate or tangled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pessimists sit in his complicated set-up beyond the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' gives NIHIISTS, and 'outside' wraps it around L; Lima is the NATO alphabet, not Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihilists reject moral and religious principles, believing life meaningless, so they are negative thinkers.

clue.text: Endlessly respect a Liberal naval commander

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the word for respect loses its last letter

parts.note: to admire is to respect

explanation.surface: Endlessly respect a Liberal who commands the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the most senior rank of officer in a navy, commanding a fleet.

clue.text: Woman touring hot area north of a desert

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the woman's name is placed around the next letters

parts.note: Sara is a woman's name
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A woman tours a hot area north of a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of a desert' looks like geography, but 'north' is only N and 'of a desert' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saharan is the adjective for the Sahara, the great North African desert.

clue.text: Greenness of mineral water upset over ends of table

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another comes first, above it
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the brand is read backwards

parts.note: Evian is a well-known brand of French mineral water

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters, taken from table

explanation.surface: Innocence suffers as mineral water is spilt across the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns EVIAN into NAIVE; 'ends of table' supplies TE below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenness here means inexperience or innocence, which is exactly naivety.

clue.text: Unleavened bread originally ideal with tea and a little butter

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the first letter of ideal is used

explanation.surface: Flatbread is ideally served with tea and a bit of butter.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces go in the order CHA, PAT, I, regardless of the order in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat Indian bread made without yeast, so it is unleavened bread.

clue.text: French novelist briefly keeping island bird

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the shortened name holds the island letter inside it
briefly means cut short, so the novelist loses her last letter

parts.note: Colette was a French novelist, author of Gigi

explanation.surface: A French writer, briefly holding an island, keeps a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims COLETTE to COLETT, which takes I inside it before the last T.
explanation.definitionFit: The coletit, more often coal tit, is a small European songbird of the tit family.

clue.text: Become tedious letter-writer, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is chosen for how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: St Paul wrote many of the New Testament epistles, or letters

explanation.surface: A dull correspondent, as far as one can tell from hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostle Paul is the great letter-writer of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To pall is to lose interest or appeal through familiarity, so it means become tedious.

clue.text: Philosopher with authority becomes factory designer

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher
a right is an entitlement or authority to act

explanation.surface: A thinker granted authority turns into a designer of factories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link but is W.
explanation.definitionFit: A millwright designs, builds and maintains mills and their machinery, so is a factory designer.

clue.text: Travel round America, having time and energy

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the travel word goes around the following letters

parts.note: to go is to travel
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: Travelling around America with time and energy to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' wraps the travel word around UST; 'energy' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enthusiasm and vigour, so it means energy.

clue.text: Smear second book excluded from promotional hype

indicators.note: excluded from means left out of, so one letter is removed from the hype

parts.note: a blurb is promotional text, as on a book jacket
B is the abbreviation for book; second says which of two Bs goes

explanation.surface: A smear campaign leaves out the second volume from the publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: BLURB has two Bs; the second one is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is a smudge or smear, as on a drawing or a lens.

clue.text: Tough soldiers tight-lipped about start of invasion

parts.note: the RE, Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for tight-lipped goes around the next letter

parts.note: silent means saying nothing, tight-lipped

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from invasion

explanation.surface: Hardy soldiers keep quiet as the invasion begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the invasion's first letter inside the tight-lipped word; RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means able to withstand hardship and recover, so tough.

clue.text: Follow Europe's directions to return

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: EU is short for the European Union, with the S from the apostrophe S
N and E are compass directions

explanation.surface: Follow Europe's instructions to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' reads as instructions but gives compass points; EUS NE backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards as a result, so to follow.

clue.text: Stealthy new Tories stir up unions at first

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the following letters are re-formed in a different order
at first means only the opening letter of unions is used

explanation.surface: Covert Tories are stirring up the trade unions from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' scrambles TORIES STIR UP plus U from 'unions at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreptitious means done secretly so as not to be noticed, so stealthy.
